clue.text: Ambitious young doctor's problematic late one-year drug test

indicators.note: something problematic is in disorder, so the fodder letters are rearranged

parts.note: one is I, the Roman numeral, and Y is the usual abbreviation for year

explanation.surface: A keen junior medic finds a drug trial running a year late and troubled.
explanation.walkthrough: 'problematic' rearranges LATE, IY, DRUG and TEST. Tertius Lydgate is the idealistic young doctor in George Eliot's Middlemarch.
explanation.definitionFit: Lydgate arrives in Middlemarch as an ambitious newly qualified physician full of reforming plans.

clue.text: Barbara, a writer using deception with language

parts.note: a trap is a trick or deception
Ido is an artificial language derived from Esperanto

explanation.surface: A woman author practises trickery with words.
explanation.walkthrough: Ido is a constructed language, a reformed Esperanto. Barbara Trapido is a South African-born British novelist.
explanation.definitionFit: Barbara Trapido is a novelist, author of Brother of the More Famous Jack.

clue.text: Actor who played a Roman emperor, king and US President

definitions.text: Actor who played a Roman emperor

parts.note: rex is Latin for king
Benjamin and William Henry Harrison were both US presidents

explanation.surface: A performer who portrayed an emperor, a monarch and a president.
explanation.walkthrough: Rex Harrison played Julius Caesar in the 1963 film Cleopatra.
explanation.definitionFit: Rex Harrison took the part of Caesar opposite Elizabeth Taylor in Cleopatra.

clue.text: Old Testament figure seen in two different accounts

parts.note: an ISA is an Individual Savings Account, a British tax-free savings account
AC is the standard abbreviation for account

explanation.surface: A biblical character who appears in two separate versions of a story.
explanation.walkthrough: An ISA is a British tax-free savings account; 'accounts' suggests narratives but means bank accounts.
explanation.definitionFit: Abraham's son, nearly sacrificed in Genesis, is a patriarch of the Hebrew Bible.

clue.text: Boy accepting current tutor in Galloway

indicators.note: accepting means taking in, so one piece holds the other

parts.note: a son is a boy
amps measure electric current

explanation.surface: A lad takes on a Scottish teacher.
explanation.walkthrough: Dominie Sampson is the tutor in Scott's Guy Mannering, set in Galloway in south-west Scotland.
explanation.definitionFit: Dominie Sampson tutors the Bertram family in Walter Scott's novel set in Galloway.

clue.text: Yankee girls dancing around a famous tree

annotationWithheld.why: Yankee girls dancing around a famous tree: Y plus an anagram of GIRLS round A gives only seven of YGGDRASIL's nine letters; G and D are unaccounted for, so the clue as held looks misread or cut
annotationWithheld.clue: Yankee girls dancing around a famous tree

clue.text: Casually travel from Georgia to Germany

parts.note: GA is the postal abbreviation for the US state of Georgia
D is the international vehicle code for Germany

explanation.surface: Wandering idly from one country to another.
explanation.definitionFit: To gad about is to roam aimlessly in search of pleasure.

clue.text: American writer and maker of artist's products, writing article about yellow and gold

definitions.text: American writer and maker of artist's products

indicators.note: about means around, so the article wraps the colour

parts.note: the is the definite article
or is the heraldic name for gold or yellow
Au is the chemical symbol for gold

explanation.surface: An American author who also made art supplies, writing about colour.
explanation.walkthrough: Henry David Thoreau worked in his family's pencil-making business.
explanation.definitionFit: Thoreau wrote Walden and helped run his family's pencil factory, making artists' pencils.

clue.text: One in just over 1000, like The Deemster

indicators.note: the word in tells us one piece is placed inside the other here

parts.note: MX in Roman numerals is 1010, a little over a thousand
an is the indefinite article, meaning one

explanation.surface: A ranking of roughly a thousand, compared with a novel called The Deemster.
explanation.walkthrough: The Deemster is Hall Caine's novel of the Isle of Man, where a deemster is a judge.
explanation.definitionFit: The Deemster is set on the Isle of Man, so the book is of that island.

clue.text: Go and dream about the end of the world?

indicators.note: about here means turned around, so the letters of the phrase are rearranged

explanation.surface: Advice to go off and imagine how everything finishes.
explanation.walkthrough: 'about' rearranges the ten letters of GO AND DREAM.
explanation.definitionFit: The final battle at the close of history in the Book of Revelation gives its name to any catastrophe.

clue.text: Right to become fashionable in a European country's capital

indicators.note: one letter is to become another, so a piece of the word is swapped out

parts.note: France's, with the possessive s kept as a letter
in means in fashion

explanation.surface: A political right gaining favour in the capital city of some European state.
explanation.walkthrough: In FRANCES the R ('Right') is replaced by IN ('fashionable'). 'capital' looks like a city but means money.
explanation.definitionFit: Capital in the sense of funds or money resources.

clue.text: Right-wing East German nut's a Jewish writer who studied at the LSE!

definitions.text: a Jewish writer who studied at the LSE

parts.note: R abbreviates right
Ost is the German word for east
an en is a printer's measure, also called a nut

explanation.surface: A far-right fanatic from the old East Germany turns out to be a Jewish author.
explanation.walkthrough: Leo Rosten, author of The Joys of Yiddish, studied at the London School of Economics. In printing, an en space is sometimes called a nut.
explanation.definitionFit: Leo Rosten was a Jewish-American humorist and author who spent time studying at the London School of Economics.

clue.text: Poem metaphorically expressing love between a mathematician and articulate cavalier

parts.note: one who sums or adds up figures is jokingly a summer

indicators.note: articulate means spoken out, so the next word is given by its sound

parts.note: a cavalier is a mounted gentleman soldier, a knight

explanation.surface: A love poem bridging a numbers person and a well-spoken Royalist.
explanation.walkthrough: SUMMER is 'one who sums'. 'articulate' turns KNIGHT into the word that sounds the same. Auden's A Summer Night celebrates a moment of shared love.
explanation.definitionFit: Auden's poem of that title describes a vision of agape, love among friends, through the imagery of a June evening.

clue.text: Disappointing in two ways, end of long second version of a gothic novel from a Scot

definitions.text: version of a gothic novel from a Scot

parts.note: poor and thin both mean disappointing or inadequate
thin, as in a thin excuse, is a second word for disappointing

indicators.note: end of picks the final letter of the word long

explanation.surface: A let-down rewrite of a gothic tale by a Scottish author.
explanation.definitionFit: Alasdair Gray, a Scot, wrote a reworking of Frankenstein under this title.

clue.text: Beastly accommodation that's seen in Hard Times

definitions.meaning: a hart is a male deer, so a dwelling for one is a beast's lodging
James ... is the idle gentleman who appears in Dickens's novel Hard Times

explanation.surface: A stable for animals turns up in a Dickens novel.
explanation.definitionFit: Harthouse is a character in Dickens's Hard Times; split, it reads as a deer's dwelling.

clue.text: Scandal about a girl in a famous Victorian poem

definitions.text: girl in a famous Victorian poem

indicators.note: about means around, so one piece goes round the other

parts.note: mud, as in mud-slinging, is scandalous talk

explanation.surface: Gossip surrounds the heroine of a celebrated nineteenth-century poem.
explanation.definitionFit: Tennyson's monodrama names its heroine in its title, the girl invited to come into the garden.

clue.text: Immodest content in some poetry

indicators.note: the contents of the word Immodest hold the answer inside it

explanation.surface: Shameless material found in certain verse.
explanation.definitionFit: Lyric poems addressed to a subject are a kind of verse.

clue.text: Writer of radio plays

indicators.note: the letters are made to play, moving into a new order

explanation.surface: Someone who wrote dramas for broadcast.
explanation.walkthrough: 'plays' rearranges OF RADIO. Dario Fo was an Italian playwright and Nobel laureate.
explanation.definitionFit: Dario Fo was an Italian playwright who won the Nobel Prize in Literature.

clue.text: Loathing about an abrupt 21 lady in the money

parts.note: re means about, concerning

indicators.note: in places one piece inside another here

parts.note: pence are British coins, money

indicators.note: abrupt means cut short, so a final letter is lopped off

parts.note: 21 refers to the answer French; elle is the French word for she, a lady

explanation.surface: Disgust at a curt Frenchwoman who has struck it rich.
explanation.walkthrough: '21' points to the answer at 21-across, so the lady is French: elle, 'she'. 'abrupt' cuts her short, and 'in the money' means inside old British pennies.
explanation.definitionFit: Repellence is the quality of repelling, the strong aversion felt towards something.

clue.text: Request about boundary without a guarantee

indicators.note: about places one piece around the other
without takes the following letter out of the word

parts.note: a plea is an appeal or request
an edge is a border or boundary

explanation.surface: Asking for a border with no warranty attached.
explanation.walkthrough: 'without' drops the A and 'about' wraps the rest round the boundary. 'guarantee' is the legal noun: the person to whom a guaranty is given, not the promise itself.
explanation.definitionFit: In law a guarantee can be the party who receives a promise of security, just as a pledgee receives a pawned item.

clue.text: Wealthy Victorian rogue using a vehicle to hide

parts.note: a car is a vehicle
to bury something is to hide it

explanation.surface: A rich nineteenth-century scoundrel uses a car to stash his loot.
explanation.walkthrough: Sir Felix Carbury is the dissolute baronet of Trollope's The Way We Live Now.
explanation.definitionFit: Sir Felix Carbury is a titled cad in Trollope's satire of Victorian high society.

clue.text: Swearing in a foreign language?

parts.note: bad language is excused with 'pardon my' plus the name of a European tongue

explanation.surface: Cursing in a tongue that is not your own.
explanation.definitionFit: The phrase 'pardon my French' apologises for swearing, treating curses as a foreign tongue.

clue.text: Town with a castle relies on ruins (old style)

indicators.note: ruins means wrecks, so the letters are broken up and rearranged

explanation.surface: A fortified town depends on its old ruins.
explanation.walkthrough: 'ruins' rearranges RELIES ON. '(old style)' tells us the spelling is the old English one, not modern Danish Helsingør.
explanation.definitionFit: Elsinore is the old English name of the Danish town of Kronborg Castle, Hamlet's setting.

clue.text: Talks round authority

parts.note: says means talks or speaks
O is round in shape

explanation.surface: Discussion about who is in charge.
explanation.definitionFit: Someone's say-so is their permission or authority.

clue.text: Gaunt boy on treatment — a patent medicine

indicators.note: treatment means handling, so the letters are worked into a new order

explanation.surface: A thin lad undergoing a course of a proprietary remedy.
explanation.walkthrough: 'treatment' rearranges GAUNT BOY ON. Tono-Bungay is the bogus tonic in H. G. Wells's novel of that name.
explanation.definitionFit: In H. G. Wells's novel it is a worthless proprietary tonic sold through advertising.

clue.text: An evil monster caught by men

parts.note: OR, other ranks, means ordinary soldiers or men
C is the cricket abbreviation for caught

explanation.surface: A villainous beast captured by soldiers.
explanation.definitionFit: Orcs are brutish goblin creatures of Tolkien's fiction.

clue.text: Welsh product that's more than tacky

definitions.meaning: Irvine Welsh, the Scottish author of Trainspotting, wrote a novel of this name
an adhesive is stickier than something merely tacky

explanation.surface: A Welsh export that is worse than tasteless.
explanation.walkthrough: Welsh is the novelist Irvine Welsh, not the nation; the novel Glue followed Trainspotting.
explanation.definitionFit: An adhesive sticks firmly, beyond being slightly tacky; Irvine Welsh also published a novel with that title.

clue.text: The Mouse's Tale is such a definite versifier's effort

parts.note: concrete means definite, specific
a versifier produces poetry

explanation.surface: Lewis Carroll's mouse tells a tale that is plainly a piece of verse.
explanation.walkthrough: The Mouse's Tale in Alice's Adventures in Wonderland is printed in the winding shape of a tail.
explanation.definitionFit: Verse laid out on the page as a picture of its subject is shape poetry, as Carroll's tail-shaped tale is.
